subject: [AMBER] How to Compare RDFs for different systems

messages.author: Matthew Guberman-Pfeffer
messages.body:
Dear Amber Community,
I want to compute the radial distribution function for solvent relative to a cofactor for a monomeric and dimeric protein system. I don’t fully understand the comments about the care needed for normalization at
https://amberhub.chpc.utah.edu/radial-rdf/
<
https://amberhub.chpc.utah.edu/radial-rdf/
>. My two systems have different numbers of solvent molecules, but if the raw RDF is normalized for each system with the default density value in CPPTRAJ, why would the two RDFs not be comparable? Or, put another way, how can you compute RDFs for two systems with different numbers of solvent molecules so that they can be compared?
Best,
Matthew

messages.author: Thomas Cheatham
messages.body:
I did not read the comments (which really I should have so I did and wow is that tutorial daunting and I will push to soften and provide basic intro) but the normalization in my experience is do not compare apples to oranges - if both plots normalize to unity (1.0) you are OK in quantitative comparison, if not, can compare peak locations but not peak heights.
--tec3
